He has club friends — loud Takashi and cosplayer Yumi — but no romance experience and no wish for any.

One Thursday the department’s most popular gal, Hamazaki Risa (a blunt, teasing Amane-Kei-style gal), spots the new Shield Hero episode on his phone mid-lecture. Within a month she boldly escalates: an Akihabara pop-up (and a cat-ear headband “joke gift”), a late-night “Your Name” screening in Shinjuku where she cries, karaoke for two, library dates, and a Sunday at the Odaiba anime convention with matching keychains — always respecting his need for “cave days”.

Months later they are close friends who meet several times a week. Risa has fallen for him and turns uncharacteristically shy: her first visit to his apartment in October, a November convention, Christmas illuminations by Tokyo Tower. Yumi sees through her; Takashi can’t believe Eon is friends with someone “campus level”. On a snowy January hotpot night Risa half-confesses — “I like spending time with you. A lot.” — and the still-dense Eon answers that he values her too. The saga ends with their friendship deepening and Risa patiently waiting for him to see her the way she sees him.
